newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FedEx to set up Taiwan express hub.
newsitem.headline: FedEx to set up Taiwan express hub.

text.p: Taiwan's aeronautics authority said on Monday it has reached initial agreement with U.S. firm Federal Express Corp, in which the latter has agreed to set up an express cargo transshipment centre in Taiwan.

"We have reached agreement with FedEx in major items, and we hope both sides can make final settlement in minor items on Monday or Tuesday," Tsai Tui, head of the Civil Aeronautics Administration (CAA) under the communications ministry, told Reuters.
"If both sides can reach agreement in minor items, the two have temporarily scheduled to sign an agreement on January 7," he said by telephone.
If all goes smoothly, FedEx plans to start operations for its Taiwan hub sometime in 1997, Tsai said.
He declined to give more details. "I also cannot reveal how much money FedEx plans for the investment," Tsai said.
FedEx has expressed willingness to set up an express transshipment centre in the Taipei international airport.
In June, another U.S. firm United Parcel Service signed accords with the CAA to build a $400 million Asian express transshipment centre at Taipei's international airport.
The UPS hub would act as a transshipment centre for processing express parcels entering northeast and southeast Asia from other parts of the world, officials said then.
Opening of such a centre on the island would provide a boost to Taiwan's drive to establish itself as an attractive base for international firms' regional operations centres.
